glosses: To have or give off a strong, unpleasant smell.
To be evidently associated with something unpleasant.

examples.text: The boss appointing his nephew as a director reeks of nepotism.

glosses: To be emitted or exhaled, emanate, as of vapour or perfume.
To emit smoke or vapour; to steam.

examples.text: […] innumerable Legions of his Angels of Light, the warm gleames of whose presence is able to make the Mountains to reek and smoak, and to awake that fiery principle that lies dormient in the Earth into a devouring flame.
The slaughter of lambs in offering reeked the fore-courts of the Temple.
[I]f we get caught we're for the gibbet and the chains. Our flesh will reek the wind.

glosses: To fall in such a way (e.g. particularly finely or heavily) as to resemble smoke.

examples.text: ... the snow still darkens the air, and reeks along the curling wreaths, as if each were a furnace.
